Hi Emily — thanks for the quick heads up. We're on this and will provide a progress update by 10:00 PT. In the meantime, two suggested mitigations on your side that are safe to apply immediately:

- Shorten client-side SSE reconnect backoff to 250ms for transient opens (so users get faster retries)
- Enable a 3-second pre-open keepalive on connections if your client supports it (helps detect partial stalls)

We'll coordinate a follow-up message for your support team with clearer language after engineering confirms root cause.

— Lauren
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:05:47 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production issue — streaming chat p99 spikes this morning

Quick technical update from triage:

- Reproduced elevated p99 on hosted SSE endpoints in us-west2 during a synthetic peak that mirrors CloudRetail traffic profile.
- Root cause (interim): a combination of a recent autoscaling policy change for the streaming runtime (reduction of aggressive scale-out threshold) and a degradation in connection muxing under cold-start bursts. The scale-out window missed the initial surge, so queueing increased and first-token latency spiked.
- Upstream fallback to smaller model variants was working but didn't trigger fast enough for live sessions.

Actions taken:
- Rolled back the autoscaling policy to previous thresholds (effective 10:02 PT).
- Enabled a temporary aggressive warm pool for streaming workers for CloudRetail's tenancy for the next 2 hours.
- Pushed a hotfix to connection mux to reduce lock contention; will monitor.

Preliminary impact: p99 for stream-open dropped from ~2.2s to ~220ms within three minutes of the rollback. We'll watch for recurrence during the remainder of your campaign.

Attachments: cloudretail_kpis_april20.csv

— Marcus Lin
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@cloudretail.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:02:10 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary / next steps — CloudRetail p99 streaming regression (morning peak)

Team — final summary for the execs and for our postmortem:

- Impact: CloudRetail experienced a ~7% increased chat failure rate and p99 stream-open regression (avg spike to 2.2s) between 08:45–09:05 PT. External customers noticed increased timeouts and user friction on a high-priority campaign.
- Cause: autoscaling threshold change + connection mux lock contention under cold-start burst.
- Immediate fix: rolled back autoscaling policy; enabled warm pool for CloudRetail tenancy; deployed a hotfix to reduce mux contention. Observed rapid reduction in p99 to ~220ms.
- Customer remediation: Lauren to send a short note to CloudRetail support explaining mitigation and offering 10% usage credit for the impacted window (pending approval).
- Operational follow-ups (owners):
  - SRE (Rachel): Full infra metric capture and retention for 24 hours; publish timeline.
  - Runtime eng (Marcus): Root-cause PR and regression test to prevent similar mux contention under cold starts.
  - CS (Lauren/Aditya): Customer-facing postmortem and credit approval flow.
  - Product: Evaluate autoscaler default thresholds and introduce canary gating for policy changes.

Requesting executive sign-off on the proposed 10% credit for CloudRetail (estimate $6.4k) and permission to open an expedited incident postmortem with Product.

Aditya Rao
Head of Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference
